scenes.title: Start with the application and environment

captions.text: Before taking over a command workstation, check which application
and environment you are using.
We begin in IC's Calls workspace, with the department's training
incidents already listed.
Open the menu at the upper left and choose Settings.
At the top, App Info shows App Name, Version and Environment; this example
identifies Resgrid IC in development.
That gives a command aide useful details when reporting a problem.
For practice, locate those three values, then find the Account section
directly underneath before reviewing connection or sign-in settings.

This is metadata correspondence review, not new original-pixel, encoded-frame, browser-playback or User listening.

captions.text: In Settings, Account, open Server to inspect the connection address.
The form shows Custom and a complete Server URL; the loopback
address here belongs to this local training environment.
Use the address supplied by your administrator for your own installation.
The note says to leave off the API version path and a trailing slash.
Cancel closes this review without saving a different server.
During a command handover, comparing the address first helps avoid
troubleshooting the wrong installation.
Practice finding the complete address rather than relying
on the shortened Account row.

read Confirm Logout.
The warning says logout will clear app data, cached values and settings.
Choose Cancel to finish this review while keeping the session; an actual
logout is a separate decision.
The same checks help a fire or EMS command aide, a community crisis
coordinator, a search-and-rescue lead, a security supervisor, a wildland command
team or an industrial response desk.
In each setting, a useful handover names the environment, account
state and current queue rather than leaving the next operator to guess.
